EPMC:PMC:PMC3102942.setting: Planned multiple case study of foot and ankle surgeons (School of Public Health, Queensland University of Technology)

cycle1.result: not reported

EPMC:PMC:PMC3102942.other_findings: Research protocol: semi-structured interviews planned with a purposive sample of 6 to 8 surgeons from 3 to 4 specialities to explore attitudes and behaviours towards the audit cycle.

PMID:27499414.setting: Two Western Cape tertiary referral hospitals (HY and HG), elective total hip replacement

cycle1.result: Transfusion rate 41.6% at HY v. 10.0% at HG (overall 25.8%). Of 120 patients with complete data, 113 (94.2%) had a blood bank order; 102/113 (90.3%) were group-and-screen and 29/113 (25.7%) were converted to full crossmatch.

PMID:27499414.other_findings: Females had a higher transfusion rate than males (33.0% v. 15.0%, p<0.05). Authors recommend a Hb trigger of 8.0 g/dL and group-and-screen rather than routine crossmatch.

PMID:24352825.setting: Dorset County Hospital, primary or revision total hip or knee arthroplasty under an enhanced recovery programme

cycle1.result: Mechanical prophylaxis only: DVT 0.73% (95% CI 0.37-1.43%), PE 0.91% (95% CI 0.49-1.67%).

PMID:24352825.intervention: Chemical prophylaxis (enoxaparin) added to mechanical prophylaxis.

cycle2.result: DVT 0.57% (95% CI 0.20-1.68%), PE 1.15% (95% CI 0.53-2.48%); no statistically significant difference in symptomatic VTE.

PMID:24352825.other_findings: Authors question the role of routine pharmacological prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty under enhanced recovery.

PMID:37262373.setting: Neurological focused care unit, Midwest tertiary care centre, lumbar laminectomy patients

cycle1.result: Retrospective chart audit showed documentation of mobility at 24 and 48 hours was lacking (no figures given).

PMID:37262373.intervention: Staff education with a self-paced module on benefits of mobility and EMR documentation, including the Johns Hopkins Highest Level of Mobility scale and 6-clicks scale.

cycle2.result: Improved documentation of early mobilised patients (no figures given).

PMID:37262373.other_findings: Plan-Do-Check-Act model used; further chart reviews planned to assess sustainability.

PMID:23857572.setting: Single-surgeon veterinary practice (Calder Vets), tibial tuberosity advancement in dogs
PMID:23857572.standard: Pre-defined target major complication rate monitored with CUSUM quality boundaries

cycle1.result: Major complications in 15 of 167 procedures (9%) within 12 months; learning curve continued until the 22nd procedure.

PMID:23857572.other_findings: After the learning curve the target complication rate was re-set lower and performance stayed within the revised boundary.

PMID:27496722.setting: Addenbrooke's Hospital, Major Trauma Centre, Cambridge
PMID:27496722.standard: Cambridge Polytrauma Pathway (Early Appropriate Care) devised from NCEPOD guidelines and literature

cycle1.result: 8 patients received definitive orthopaedic intervention out-of-hours; other baseline figures not reported.

PMID:27496722.intervention: Cambridge Polytrauma Pathway: consultant MDT decisions in critical care unit, early full body trauma CT, serial lactate and fibrinogen, out-of-hours theatre reserved for life-and-limb threatening injuries.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in recording of lactate and fibrinogen on admission (p<0.000, p=0.015) and preoperatively (p=0.003, p=0.030). Time to CT unchanged (p=0.536), median 0.53h (IQR 0.48-0.75). Out-of-hours definitive orthopaedic intervention fell from 8 to zero (p=0.195).

PMID:27496722.other_findings: Early daytime MDT decision-making adopted; GOS-E or EQ-5D recommended for outcome assessment.

PMID:21781124.setting: Tertiary hospital, cardiothoracic and orthopaedic surgical patients (QEII Medical Centre, Western Australia)

cycle1.result: 36.5% had preoperative iron studies; of those, 38.5% had anaemia of inflammation, 21.5% IDA, 23.1% normal. 51.5% of patients transfused post-surgery had a discharge Hb ≥110 g/l.

PMID:21781124.other_findings: Iron studies were more often requested postoperatively; restricting discharge Hb to 90 or 100 g/l may have avoided transfusion in 14.8-42.6% of patients.

PMID:36507202.setting: Sir H. N. Reliance Foundation Hospital, Mumbai, tertiary care centre; typed EMR operative proforma
PMID:36507202.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice guidelines (2014)

cycle1.result: 100% for date/time, surgeon, procedure, extra procedure; operative diagnosis 99.35%; antibiotic prophylaxis 99.35; incision 94.77%; findings 92.16%; prosthesis 97.37%; DVT prophylaxis 96.08%; post-op instructions 93.46%; tourniquet time 41.83%; blood loss 59.48%; closure 16.99%; complications 51.63%; elective/emergency setting 0%.

PMID:36507202.other_findings: Mandated EMR fields were well documented; authors suggest mandating further fields to improve documentation.

PMID:27001132.topic: Non-traumatic spinal cord injury rehabilitation outcomes
PMID:27001132.setting: National Spinal Injuries Centre, Stoke Mandeville Hospital, tertiary spinal cord injury rehabilitation unit

cycle1.result: Degenerative vertebral column disorders, infection and vascular disorders accounted for 80% of NTSCI; infection-related NTSCI had the highest needs.

PMID:27001132.other_findings: Relationship between cause and rehabilitation outcome may be mediated by injury severity.

PMID:27655773.standard: ACL reconstruction within 12 months of injury

cycle1.result: Mean time from injury to surgery 14 months (range 3-56).

PMID:27655773.intervention: Acute Knee Clinic established in December 2004.

cycle2.result: 21 Acute Knee Clinic patients: mean 6 months to surgery, 95% within 12 months; 28 elective clinic patients: mean 25 months, 53% within 12 months.

PMID:27655773.other_findings: 90% of A&E referrals were seen by a specialist within four weeks (May 2005 to July 2007); the clinic accounted for only 40% of ACL reconstruction referrals.

PMID:12486988.topic: Hip fracture process of care standards
PMID:12486988.setting: Seven hospitals with trauma orthopaedic departments, East Anglia (multi-site audit)
PMID:12486988.standard: Indicator standards for re-audit circulated after the 1992 audit

cycle1.result: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 45%; early mobilisation 56%.

PMID:12486988.intervention: Results of the 1992 audit and indicator standards circulated to orthopaedic and care of the elderly consultants and audit leads at each hospital.

cycle2.result: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 81%; early mobilisation 70%; reduced pneumonia, wound infection, pressure sores and fatal PE.

PMID:12486988.other_findings: No change in 3-month functional outcome or mortality; some hospitals failed to maintain good practice.

PMID:8785639.setting: Clinical Radiology Department, St James's University Hospital, Leeds, large acute hospital
PMID:8785639.standard: NRPB recommendation that CT be clinically justified by an experienced radiologist

cycle1.result: Of 915 examinations for benign disease, 293 (32%) were orthopaedic, including 255 (87%) for back pain; no substantial numbers of inappropriate CT found.

PMID:8785639.other_findings: CT for benign non-orthopaedic disease in 97 women under 50, 49 reported normal; MRI substitution for spine CT suggested.

PMID:42134925.setting: UK GP surgery (Mid and South Essex)
PMID:42134925.standard: NICE CG161/NG5 and NHS England guidance: documented medication review within 4 weeks after a fall; target 100%

cycle1.result: 22% (14/63) documented review within 4 weeks.

PMID:42134925.intervention: Clinician education on NICE guidance, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews.
PMID:42134925.other_findings: More appropriate deprescribing, particularly of benzodiazepines, anticholinergics and antihypertensives.

PMID:29212692.topic: Major orthopaedic trauma in older people
PMID:29212692.setting: Trauma Audit Research Network database, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 72,942 of 142,765 adults (51.09%) had long bone or pelvic fractures; 30-day mortality 6.8% in older v. 2.5% in younger; critical care episodes 9.7% v. 18.2%.

PMID:29212692.other_findings: Older patients were often managed by surgeons in isolation; authors call for shared orthogeriatric care models.

PMID:40826210.topic: Fascia iliaca block for hip fracture
PMID:40826210.setting: Emergency departments, Royal University Hospital, Saskatoon (University of Saskatchewan)
PMID:40826210.standard: Target fascia iliaca block in 50% of hip fracture patients within 18 months

cycle1.result: Baseline fascia iliaca block rate 2.0%; 6 physicians performing it.

PMID:40826210.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: educational materials and standardised equipment carts; staff and trainee education sessions; further education, audit and feedback, and incentives.

cycle2.result: Fascia iliaca block rate 22.6%; 35 physicians performing it; special cause variation (shift) on SPC chart.

PMID:40826210.other_findings: Target of 50% not met; one adverse event (arterial puncture) without significant harm.

PMID:39961162.setting: UK-FATE national prospective audit, 68 UK centres

cycle1.result: Symptomatic VTE after ATR 3.69% (n = 40) v. 0.57% (n = 59) after other foot and ankle surgery.

PMID:39961162.other_findings: No significant difference in VTE by chemical prophylaxis, weight-bearing or immobilisation strategy; VTE patients were older.

PMID:41108795.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit data, Scottish hospitals

cycle1.result: 9867 (72%) received SHS; no significant difference in 30-day (OR 1.05) or 60-day (OR 1.10) survival; lower early mobilisation with IMN (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.59-0.70).

PMID:41108795.other_findings: SHS associated with early mobilisation, reduced length of stay and likely lower cost.

PMID:31094799.setting: Gold Coast Hospital and Health Service, 2-campus tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: 79% compliance with national guidelines; orthopaedics used most cases (22.9%, n = 108).

PMID:31094799.other_findings: Highest average return in vascular surgery (699 mL) and urology (654 mL); revision (7.6%) and primary (6.6%) THR among most common procedures.

PMID:19527281.setting: 10 PREDICT paediatric emergency departments (clinical audit), 13 (organisational audit)

cycle1.result: 196 migraine, 197 abdominal pain, 177 femur fracture cases. Less than half had pain score at triage. Femur fractures: analgesia 78% (opioids 49%, femoral nerve blocks 40%); median 75 min to enteral and 26 min to parenteral medication.

PMID:19527281.other_findings: 92% of EDs had pain policies but only 15% had pain quality improvement programmes; femoral nerve blocks underused.

PMID:26696248.topic: Blood test requesting in acute admissions
PMID:26696248.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, NHS Tayside, Dundee; acute admissions
PMID:26696248.standard: Locally developed multidisciplinary blood requesting guidelines

cycle1.result: LFTs 895, coagulation/INR 307, CRP 894; mean 4.81 requests per patient (SD 4.75); cost £2674.14.

PMID:26696248.intervention: Clinical guidelines for blood requesting developed with multidisciplinary input and implemented in the department.
PMID:26696248.other_findings: Reduced venepuncture rates as well as cost.

PMID:32099276.setting: Journal of Clinical Orthopaedics and Trauma, SCOPUS and PubMed data

cycle1.result: Submissions increased 2.8 times and citations 16.6 times in 2019 compared with 2015; journal cited 1702 times.

PMID:32099276.other_findings: More higher level of evidence papers being published.

EPMC:CTX:C3089.setting: National Joint Registry for England and Wales

cycle1.dates: 1 April 2007 to 31 March 2008 (procedures 1 January to 31 December 2007)
cycle1.result: not reported

EPMC:CTX:C3089.other_findings: Report includes revision rates, mortality and pulmonary embolism using linked HES and PEDW data.

PMID:15574237.setting: Midfoot and forefoot surgery under ankle block (Flinders University)

cycle1.result: 3.1% complained of tourniquet pain; 0.4% converted to general anaesthesia; 97.2% would have surgery again with an ankle tourniquet.

PMID:15574237.other_findings: Tourniquet pain associated with age and tourniquet time; patients 70 or older had 3.5 times more tourniquet pain.

PMID:16278179.setting: Department of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery, University of Oulu

cycle1.result: 63% of surgeries delayed more than 24 hours; all received LMWH; 92% received antibiotic prophylaxis; deep infection 2.5%.

PMID:16278179.other_findings: Describes the extended SAHFE data set; function significantly impaired at four months.

PMID:38677960.setting: Emergency departments, national audit of public trauma hospitals
PMID:38677960.standard: Pre-defined audit criteria for AP and axillary/Velpeau views

cycle1.result: Two views in 75.92% (n = 599); axillary or Velpeau view in 21.17% (n = 167); AP view met audit criteria in 23.09% (n = 181).

PMID:38677960.other_findings: Surgeon survey (70.8% response): 88.2% favoured three views and 94% a national protocol.

PMID:12209036.setting: Rheumatology follow-up clinics in 10 West Midlands units
PMID:12209036.standard: National Osteoporosis Society 1998 guidance; 80% of eligible patients on appropriate therapy

cycle1.result: 148 (63%) on appropriate osteoporosis medication; 202 (86%) on any treatment; DXA in 102 (43.4%). Region failed the standard.

PMID:12209036.other_findings: Of 87 inappropriately treated, 71 (81.6%) under-treated and 16 (18.4%) over-treated; re-audit planned in 2 years.

PMID:28272852.setting: Groote Schuur Hospital Trauma Unit, urban tertiary trauma unit, Cape Town

cycle1.result: 7350 interpersonal violence and 3188 motor vehicle collision attendances; weekends, month-end and long weekends busier.

PMID:28272852.other_findings: Soccer matches had no significant effect on violence-related attendances.

PMID:33586032.topic: Resuscitation discussion before hip fracture surgery
PMID:33586032.setting: Rowley Bristow Unit, St Peter's Hospital, Chertsey
PMID:33586032.standard: ReSPECT form completed before operation and countersigned by a consultant

cycle1.result: ReSPECT form completion 23%; consultant signed 41%.

PMID:17635356.setting: Paediatric dental trauma clinic, Glasgow Dental Hospital

cycle1.result: Males 60% of trauma; falls 49%, sport 18%; peak age 8-11 years (43%).

PMID:12828137.setting: Angus, Dundee Teaching Hospitals and Perth & Kinross Trusts, Tayside
PMID:12828137.standard: Previously agreed standards for administration of antibiotic prophylaxis (three general standards)

cycle1.result: Prophylaxis given to 82% of eligible orthopaedic patients; rate for indicated operations 84% to 93% across trusts; continued <24 h in 78% to 97%; given within two hours in >95%; second doses in 5/44 (11%) of operations >2 h.

PMID:12828137.other_findings: Trust comparison confined to six common procedures (166 operations) because results were sensitive to case mix.

cycle1.result: After adjustment, significant differences in post-fracture walking ability and mortality between centres but not in place of residence.

PMID:15544081.other_findings: Use of sliding hip screw v. Gamma Nail differed most between hospitals.

PMID:10986371.setting: Alexandra Hospital, Redditch, district general hospital, A&E department
PMID:10986371.standard: Transfer from A&E to ward within 1 hour

cycle1.result: Mean transfer time 2 h 45 min ± 57 min (median 2 h 40 min); 3/104 within 1 hour.

PMID:10986371.intervention: Fast tracking protocol for transfer of hip fracture patients from A&E to ward, implemented December 1997.

cycle2.result: Mean 1 h 32 min ± 40.87 min (median 1 h 25 min), p<0.001; 24/90 within 1 hour, p<0.001.

PMID:10986371.other_findings: 10 of 100 patients not fast tracked (multiple injuries, medical problems, unclear diagnosis) averaged 2 h 55 min in A&E.

PMID:35459545.setting: Gold Coast Public Hospital emergency departments

cycle1.result: 1512 presentations (56.4%) required orthopaedic management; lacerations 37.9%, ligament injury 21.3%, fractures 12.2%.

PMID:28442206.topic: MRSA eradication and antibiotic prophylaxis in hip fracture surgery
PMID:28442206.setting: Royal Liverpool Hospital, UK major trauma centre, emergency hip fracture surgery
PMID:28442206.standard: Local MRSA guidelines: eradication therapy and correct induction antibiotics for MRSA-unknown patients

cycle1.result: Eradication therapy prescribed 1%; correct antibiotic choice 18%. Operation median 24.05 h from admission but MRSA swab results at median 48 h.

PMID:28442206.intervention: Posters on induction antibiotics in anaesthetic rooms and stickers on MRSA eradication therapy on nursing care bundles.

cycle2.result: Eradication therapy prescribed 8%; correct antibiotic choice 94%.

PMID:28442206.other_findings: Eradication therapy compliance stayed poor despite stickers.

PMID:36317353.setting: 18 Scottish hospitals; linked Scottish Hip Fracture Audit and national blood transfusion data

cycle1.result: Transfusion rate 28.7% (n = 6,685); inter-hospital range 16.6% to 37.4%.

PMID:36317353.other_findings: Transfusion associated with adverse outcomes, most likely reflecting perioperative anaemia.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3103036.topic: Clinical photography in foot ulcer monitoring
EPMC:PMC:PMC3103036.setting: High Risk Foot Clinic, Liverpool Hospital, NSW

cycle1.result: 731 charts had a photograph; 623 (85%) of good quality. Probe to bone completed 99%, antibiotic 97%, offloading device 81%, Texas classification 76%.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3103036.other_findings: Completion followed item position on the form; commonest photography error was not using macro setting.

PMID:36694385.setting: Physiotherapy-led primary care musculoskeletal service, York and Scarborough

cycle1.result: 58 of 102 patients without hydrodistension required onward orthopaedic referral.

PMID:36694385.intervention: Physiotherapist-performed ultrasound-guided hydrodistension introduced to the frozen shoulder pathway in 2017.

cycle2.result: 6 of 102 patients receiving hydrodistension required onward orthopaedic referral.

PMID:32007403.setting: Two trauma and orthopaedic wards, London hospital

cycle1.result: 17 (43%) rated sleep poor; 19 (46%) said sleep affected recovery; noise main disruptor (n = 26, 65%).

PMID:32007403.other_findings: Authors call for a standardised sleep assessment and audit tool.

PMID:29339298.setting: Orthopaedics Department, Centro Hospitalar de São João, Porto, university hospital

cycle1.result: Compared with control, fluoroquinolone use fell by 2.3 DDD/1000 patient-days per month (95% CI -3.97 to -0.63); penicillin use rose by 103.3 DDD/1000 patient-days at implementation then declined (slope -5.2).

PMID:29339298.intervention: Prospective audit and feedback antimicrobial stewardship intervention starting 1 January 2015.
PMID:29339298.other_findings: Controlled interrupted time series; intervention reduced antibiotic exposure and spectrum in osteoarticular and prosthetic joint infections.

PMID:26940645.setting: UK Anaesthesia Sprint Audit of Practice data with linked outcomes

cycle1.result: Mortality 165/11,085 (1.5%) at 5 days and 563/11,085 (5.1%) at 30 days; not associated with anaesthetic technique; risk rose as blood pressure fell.

PMID:26940645.other_findings: Higher spinal bupivacaine volume weakly correlated with larger falls in systolic blood pressure.
